<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19142>

Martin Maechler (<mailto:maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch|maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch>) changed:

           What    |Removed                     |Added
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                 CC|                            |maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch

--- Comment #2 from Martin Maechler (<mailto:maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch|maechler@stat.math.ethz.ch>) ---
Well, given that in so many places people grep for the error message,
such a change would cost quite a bit of human time fixing all these instances.

Also, note that  `"a"`  _is_ a character vector length one,
so "character vector" is correct.
If we'd write the function from scratch today, I'd simply use "character"
instead 
(as all "character" are atomic vector, even if of length 0 or 1, see above),
but given the human time above, I don't think we should change it now.

Also (your '2.') the "suggestion" of _any_ character vector is really not true,
in the context of R (or programming in general, outside of language
processing).
It is typical notably for this function that not every string / character
vector will match, and given that an error is a desired outcome for
non-matching input,

I propose to close this with something as 'WORKSFORME' or 'WONTFIX'.

--- Comment #3 from Michael Chirico (<mailto:michaelchirico4@gmail.com|michaelchirico4@gmail.com>) ---
I just want to make sure my intent here is understood. I don't mean to argue
that "character vector" is incorrect, rather that it could be more helpful.

A more minimal change would be to just edit "character vector" to "character
string" in the `isFALSE(several.ok)` case, for example.

We could also simply omit the 'or NULL' part from the error message in the
patch; this would still lead to some CRAN churn, but less [1].

I don't think we should be _too_ beholden to what CRAN authors mistakenly (IMHO
[2] [3]) hard-code in their test suites if we can substantially improve the R
user experience. The proposed error is self-documenting -- the user immediately
sees how to proceed.

[1] E.g.
<https://github.com/search?q=org%3Acran+%2Fmust+be+NULL+or+a+character%2F+path%3Atest+-path%3A_snaps&type=code>.
I'm of course happy to quantify this more formally if requested.

[2] data.table, for example, takes great pains to _only_ test error messages
_under its control_:
<https://github.com/Rdatatable/data.table/blob/e26cf1b6b95474d90d3db462409e2d59e371b740/inst/tests/tests.Rraw#L200-L225>

[3] I myself have just this month had to update a CRAN package because of a
change to R's own messages, a fragility of my own making:
<https://github.com/r-lib/bit64/commit/b4f08213072de64f9b0448582290605ce7f4ab01>

*[Bug 19143] New: `Sys.getlocale()` does not mark non-ASCII Windows locale names as UTF-8*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19143>

            Bug ID: 19143
           Summary: `Sys.getlocale()` does not mark non-ASCII Windows
                    locale names as UTF-8
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Windows GUI / Window specific
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

Created attachment 3802
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3802&action=edit>
Candidate patch.

## Summary

On recent Windows systems, R uses UCRT with UTF-8 as the native encoding.
The narrow `setlocale()` result is consequently encoded as UTF-8.  Windows
locale names are not necessarily ASCII; for example, the canonical name of
the Norwegian Bokmål locale can contain `Bokmål`.

`Sys.getlocale()` returns such a name with UTF-8 bytes but does not declare
the returned R string as UTF-8.  `Encoding()` therefore reports `"unknown"`.
The return value of `Sys.setlocale()` is constructed in the same way and has
the same issue.

## Reproduction

Run this on a recent Windows system where `l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]]` is true:

```
local({
    old <- Sys.getlocale("LC_TIME")
    on.exit(Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", old))

    set <- Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "Norwegian_Norway.UTF-8")
    current <- Sys.getlocale("LC_TIME")

    print(list(
        set_value = set,
        set_encoding = Encoding(set),
        get_value = current,
        get_encoding = Encoding(current),
        get_raw = charToRaw(current),
        l10n = l10n_info()
    ))
})
```

The exact canonical spelling can vary with the Windows version.  An affected
result contains a non-ASCII spelling such as one of:

```
Norwegian (Bokmål)_Norway.utf8
Norwegian Bokmål_Norway.utf8
```

The UTF-8 representation of `å` includes the bytes `c3 a5`, but the current
result is:

```
Encoding(current)
# [1] "unknown"
```

The same is true of the value returned by `Sys.setlocale()`.

## Expected behavior

For a non-ASCII locale name returned as UTF-8, both functions should return
a string for which:

```
Encoding(current)
# [1] "UTF-8"
```

ASCII locale names should remain unmarked, in accordance with R's existing
rule that ASCII strings never carry an encoding declaration.

## Cause

`do_getlocale()` in `src/main/platform.c` obtains a narrow string from
`setlocale()` and wraps it with `mkString()`:

```
if (cat != NA_INTEGER) p = setlocale(cat, NULL);
return mkString(p ? p : "");
```

`mkString()` uses `mkChar()` and therefore records the result as
`CE_NATIVE`, even when R knows that the native locale is UTF-8.  The return
path in `do_setlocale()` similarly uses `mkChar(p)`.

The adjacent comment, `Locale specs are always ASCII`, is not valid for
Windows locale names such as Norwegian Bokmål.  UCRT can construct legacy
locale names from the English language and country names supplied by the
Windows locale APIs, and those names can contain non-ASCII characters.

This often remains unnoticed while the process stays in a UTF-8 locale,
because an unmarked string is interpreted in the current native encoding.
However, the fact that the bytes are known to be UTF-8 is lost.  This can
matter if the value outlives a subsequent locale change or is processed by
code whose encoding propagation depends on an explicit declaration.

## Proposed fix

Construct locale results with `mkCharCE(..., CE_UTF8)` whenever
`utf8locale` is true.  `mkCharCE()` already removes the declaration for
ASCII-only strings, so the change only affects non-ASCII results.

For `do_setlocale()`, copy the CRT-owned result before calling
`R_check_locale()`, since a later `setlocale()` call may invalidate the

A regression test can select `Norwegian_Norway.UTF-8` on Windows and check
the encoding of the `Sys.setlocale()` and `Sys.getlocale()` results when
UCRT expands the alias to a non-ASCII canonical name.  The test should be
conditional because that locale may not be available on every Windows
installation.

## Version information

The issue is present in current R-devel source as of 2026-08-26.  It is
relevant to UCRT-based Windows builds using UTF-8 as the native encoding,
including the default configuration on recent Windows versions.
